Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. We ran the peak-hour export and attached the matrix (senex_peak_matrix.csv) — it contains 30 days of token-level peaks broken down by region and API route. Our VP of Engineering wants to lock a tentative swap week in the first full week of October, but procurement and our ops team asked for a validation checklist and an explicit cutover window so they can coordinate maintenance windows and vendor approvals.

Concrete asks from our side:
- Can Redwood confirm the acceptance gates for throughput & tail-latency (95/99) we should use for the rightsize verification?
- Do you have a canonical sizing-validation checklist we run during the staging run (we need to map these to our readiness gates)?
- Proposed swap week: Oct 4–8 — are there any major blackout dates on your side?

I've CC'd procurement on follow-up once we have the timeline. Also including a quick note on our traffic fingerprint: most of our traffic is short chat-like requests (~30–120 tokens) with a 12% heavy-inference tail for long-batch jobs.

Attachments: senex_peak_matrix.csv (CSV, 240 KB)

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we need to surface this in our exec review on Friday.

— Maya

Maya — thanks for the export and the clarity. Tagging Ben and Grace for ops + capacity planning. Quick answers and next steps below.

Short answers:
- Acceptance gates: we recommend 95th latency under 120ms for chat routes, 99th under 450ms for long-batch endpoints (these are per-route and per-quantization-profile; Ben will confirm per-model numbers). Throughput gate is measured as sustained QPS over a 10-minute sliding window (target = 85% of committed throughput during staging).
- Checklist: attached is our internal sizing-validation-checklist.pdf. It maps to our automated smoke tests (prefix/KV cache warm, sustained QPS ramp, tail-latency sweeps, failover to a backup variant). We can annotate items that need Senex sign-off.
- Swap week: Oct 4–8 looks fine on our calendar, but we propose a dry-run on Sep 29 (staging warm-up and smoke tests) and a dark-traffic rehearsal on Oct 1 to validate routing and fallbacks.

Action items:
1) Senex: confirm procurement contact and provide SLA exception form if needed.
2) Redwood (Ben): produce per-model throughput and kv-cache warm profiles by Wed (22 Sep).
3) Redwood (Grace): create cutover runbook draft and share Drive link.

I'll schedule a 30-min ops sync for Wed 22 Sep; proposed times attached in the calendar stub.

Attachments: sizing-validation-checklist.pdf (PDF, 95 KB), proposed_cutover_window.ics (calendar stub)

Best,
Soojin Lee

Subject: Internal: Senex dedicated migration — validation plan & cutover timeline (readout)

Ben / Grace — consolidating the Senex thread and our deliverables so we have a single runbook to share tomorrow. I'm drafting the customer-facing runbook from the items below. Please review and flag anything missing.

Executive summary:
- Target swap: Oct 4–8 (customer confirmed). Dry-run: Sep 29 (staging warm-up), Rehearsal: Oct 1 (dark traffic).
- Key gates: throughput (85% sustained QPS over 10m), 95/99 latency thresholds per-route, KV cache hit-rate > 70% before cutover, successful failover to variant B without error surge during rehearsal.

Planned verification steps (runbook bullets):
1) Pre-staging (Sep 27–28): deploy dedicated model variants to staging fleet, run model-load smoke, and validate quantization parity. Owner: Ben.
2) Dry-run (Sep 29 morning): prefix warming scripts, replay 48h traffic sample on staging, capture tail-latency profiles. Stop condition: 99th latency > target for 3 continuous minutes. Owner: Ben.
3) Rehearsal (Oct 1): dark-traffic rehearsal with Senex routing team; validate NAT and egress; exercise fallback routing to hosted for 1% of traffic. Owner: Grace.
4) Acceptance window (Oct 4–5): Senex validation with Redwood on-call; isolated blue-green swap on Oct 6 with rollback plan for first 6 hours. Owner: Grace/SoE.
5) Post-cutover monitoring (Oct 6–13): elevated telemetry retention and daily readouts for first week.

Operational notes:
- Per-model throughput targets appended to this email (Ben to attach the CSV with per-model QPS targets).
- We will provide the cost-delta table for procurement by EOD tomorrow (Sep 1 — typo: meant Oct 1; Ben please confirm actual deliverable date).
- DocuSign SLA request: re-issuing link to Maya now (I'll attach before customer sync).
